prerequisites: The student has already followed courses from the first semester in phase 1.

learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to formulate a clear problem statement, objective, and assignment for electronic or ICT systems in consultation with stakeholders. He/she substantiates the assignment through analysis and research.

The student is able to develop an electronic or ICT system for a proof of concept or service based on a program of requirements. He/she is able to realize a relevant implementation of the established requirements. He/she motivates the choices made for the different components.

The student delivers a working proof of concept solution or service. The solution is a complete and correct implementation of the established requirements. He/she verifies and validates the product or service against the stated requirements. He/she documents the realization process.

The student communicates purposefully about the assignment using the main current communication forms and techniques. He/she is able to clearly summarize, verbally and in writing express, and visually present the different aspects of his/her project.

syllabus_topics: The content is project-dependent, multidisciplinary, yet has aspects that align with the various course components of the program.
During the lab sessions, students work as independently as possible on a project.
They are adequately supported by their supervisor where necessary.
They choose the subject of their project themselves.
The project proposal must be approved by the supervising lecturer before work can begin on its elaboration.
At the end of the lab series, they are asked to deliver a number of deliverables, and they get the opportunity to present and defend the results of their project.

assessment_methods.method: Practice Enterprise (theory) - Project Proposal (completeness of specification and requirements package)
Practice Enterprise (theory) - Implementation of the Version Control used
Practice Enterprise (lab) - Good operation according to specification and requirements package

assessment_rules: The assessment is based on the communicated Practise Enterprise 2 assessment framework. The Practise Enterprise (theory) accounts for 30% of the grade, while the Practise Enterprise (lab) accounts for 70%. Partial transfers are possible for successful partial results (YT6095 - Theory and YT6096 - Lab) within the academic year. Resits are possible; students should contact the supervising lecturer(s) for remediation.
